grades.quote: __sync_synchronize() is a _memory barrier_ : it tells the compiler and CPU to not reorder loads or stores across the barrier.
grades.reason: Explains that compilers and CPUs reorder loads and stores, so lock acquire and release need memory barriers to keep critical-section accesses ordered. It never mentions atomic instructions, so it supports the answer only indirectly.
Covers POSIX condition variables and mutex usage. It says nothing about memory barriers or the ordering guarantees of atomic lock instructions.

grades.quote: If the _aq_ bit is set, then no later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the AMO. Conversely, if the _rl_ bit is set, then other RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding the AMO in this RISC-V hart.
grades.reason: Shows that RISC-V AMOs give ordering only when the aq/rl bits are set. It uses an AMO spinlock whose acquire and release are marked aq and rl to order the critical section, and it says FENCE instructions are the alternative. So an atomic lock needs ordering semantics or barriers.
